public_rationale: The best observable measure of OpenAI's commitments against hyperscalers' future cloud revenue is the share of their contracted backlog. As of mid-2026, Microsoft, Oracle, Alphabet, and Amazon reported about $2.33T in combined backlog. OpenAI's commitments to Microsoft ($250B), Amazon ($138B), and Oracle (about $300B) total about $688B, roughly 29.5%, not counting its undisclosed Google contract. At Microsoft alone, OpenAI was about 45% of backlog in December and at least about 32% in June. That clears the 20% floor and sits near the low end of his 30-40% range. Microsoft's backlog also includes non-cloud software, which makes the share conservative. A caveat: OpenAI's realized revenue share is much lower today (about 7% of Microsoft's revenue), and future revenue will include sales not yet contracted.
limitations: Relies on secondary analyses rather than the filings themselves.
Treats contracted backlog as the measure of 'cloud revenues in the coming years'. A reader who means total future revenue could reach a lower share.
OpenAI contract values span different time horizons than seller backlogs.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's commitments make up at least 20%, perhaps 30-40%, of hyperscaler cloud revenues in coming years.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI is both horrendously unprofitable and has made commitments so significant that they now represent at least 20% of hyperscaler cloud revenues in the coming years, if not more like 30% to 40%.

from_speaker: at least 20% of hyperscaler cloud revenues
our_interpretation: The claim is about OpenAI's commitments as they stood at the post date (2026-08-18), measured against hyperscalers' cloud revenue in future years.

The best measure observable at the post date is contracted future revenue: OpenAI's cloud commitments as a share of the major sellers' reported backlog (remaining performance obligations). The sellers are Microsoft, Oracle, Amazon, and Alphabet.
The firm threshold is 20%. The 30-40% range is hedged ('if not more like') and is not required.
Target period: the latest backlog reports before the post (Oracle's quarter ending May 2026; the others' June 2026 quarters) through the post date.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI's commitments with the major cloud sellers equal at least 20% of their combined reported backlog as of mid-2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: OpenAI's commitments are clearly under 20% of the combined backlog, or of a reasonable estimate of those sellers' cloud revenue over the coming years.
